material: ABS and polycarbonate body with aluminium wand
features: 240 air watts — a figure measured at the cleaner head, not sealed suction
Fluffy Optic head throws a green laser across hard floors to reveal fine dust
Piezo sensor counts and sizes particles and graphs them on the LCD
Hair screw tool with a conical bar that genuinely resists long-hair wrap
Tool-free click-in battery; genuine spare is $99.99 from Dyson

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum, converts to handheld
specs.suctionRating: 240 air watts. Dyson publishes air watts, the only one of the three common numbers that describes work done at the cleaning head
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Dyson's 'up to 60 minutes' is Eco with a non-powered tool. TechGearLab measured 64 min on low and 9 min on Boost with the Digital Motorbar head fitted. Dyson publishes no per-mode table.
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — tool-free click-in battery; one included
specs.spareBattery: $99.99 for the genuine Dyson click-in pack (shared with V11, Outsize and V15s Submarine)
specs.dockOrMount: Wall-mounted docking station included; it must be screwed into a wall. No free-standing dock and no auto-empty base exists for this model
specs.filtration: Whole-machine sealed filtration with a washable lifetime filter. Dyson's 99.99%-at-0.3-micron claim is stated for Boost mode
specs.binCapacity: 0.77 L bin. Point-and-shoot ejection drives the shroud down through the bin, so your hand never goes near the dust
specs.maintenance: Filter is washable and has no replacement schedule — rinse monthly. Cleaner heads and brush bars are stocked as Dyson spares

pros: 240 air watts is a genuine cleaner-head figure, not a sealed-suction Pa number — only Samsung and Levoit publish anything comparable here
The laser head makes fine dust on hard floors visible, which changes how you clean rather than just how you feel about it
Whole-machine sealed filtration, so what the filter catches does not leak back out through the body
A genuine Dyson spare battery is $99.99 — less than half what Miele charges
cons: You hold the trigger down for the entire clean; there is no latch. This is the single most common long-term Dyson complaint
Boost mode with the powered head lasts about 9 minutes — the '60 minutes' is Eco with a non-powered tool
The dock is a wall bracket that needs drilling; there is no stand in the box and no auto-empty option at any price
$600 street and $850 list for a 0.77 L bin you still empty by hand
shortTagline: Real 240 air watts and a real laser — but 9 minutes on Boost and a trigger you must hold.

material: ABS and polycarbonate body with aluminium wand
features: Submarine wet roller head with separate 0.3 L clean and 0.36 L dirty water tanks
Same 240 air watt dry vacuum as the V15 Detect, with the laser Fluffy Optic head
Three cleaner heads in the box: Submarine, Fluffy Optic and Digital Motorbar
Drip tray included so the wet head can be parked without marking the floor
Click-in battery shared with V11, V15 and Outsize

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum with a swappable wet roller head — not a dedicated floor washer
specs.suctionRating: 240 air watts. Dyson publishes air watts rather than Pa or motor watts
specs.runtimeMax: Not published by the manufacturer — Dyson quotes only 'up to 60 minutes'
specs.runtimePoweredHead: The 60-minute figure is Eco with a non-powered tool. Dyson publishes no Boost figure and no wet-mode figure, and the Submarine head has its own motor that drains the pack faster than the dry heads
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — tool-free click-in battery. A second battery is sold separately and is not in the box
specs.spareBattery: $99.99 for the genuine Dyson click-in pack
specs.dockOrMount: Wall-mounted docking station included (drilling required), plus a drip tray for the wet head. No auto-empty, no self-clean dock
specs.filtration: Whole-machine sealed filtration; 99.99% at 0.3 micron claimed in Boost mode
specs.binCapacity: 0.77 L dust bin; the Submarine head carries 0.3 L clean water and 0.36 L dirty water
specs.maintenance: There is no self-clean cycle. The Submarine roller and both water tanks are rinsed by hand after every wet use. Replacement wet rollers are sold as Dyson spares

pros: One machine covers deep dry vacuuming and wet mopping, so you are not storing two appliances
The wet roller is genuinely effective on dried-on stains, and the two-tank design keeps dirty water off the floor
Identical 240 air watts and sealed filtration to the standard V15 Detect — the dry half is not compromised
Cheapest spare battery of any flagship here at $99.99
cons: The Submarine head is a poor vacuum: it does not pick up dry debris or large spills well, so you must vacuum first and then mop
No self-clean cycle at all — the roller and both tanks get washed by hand every time, which is exactly what a Tineco or Roborock does for you
Trigger-hold operation, and 1.5 lb heavier than the standard V15 Detect
$1,049.99 list, and the Submarine head fits no other Dyson and cannot be bought as an add-on
shortTagline: A great dry vacuum with a mop head bolted on — and no self-clean cycle at all.

material: ABS with a hinged MultiFLEX aluminium wand
features: MultiFLEX wand bends so the machine free-stands and reaches flat under furniture
DuoClean Detect nozzle with two brushrolls — soft roller plus bristle
Dirt, edge, floor-type and direction detection that actually change suction
Push-button power instead of a held trigger
5-year limited warranty on the unit, 2 years on the battery

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum, converts to handheld
specs.suctionRating: Sources conflict, and none is a suction figure: SharkNinja publishes no air watts and no Pa, describing it only as 'Shark's most powerful cordless suction' under ASTM F558 in Boost. Abt's spec sheet lists 380 W at 21.6 V, which is input power drawn, not suction delivered
specs.runtimeMax: Not published by the manufacturer — Shark quotes only 'up to 70 minutes'
specs.runtimePoweredHead: SharkNinja states the 70 minutes is ECO mode at the handheld unit — no wand, no powered floor head. Shark publishes no figure at all for Boost with the DuoClean Detect nozzle fitted
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — removable 21.6 V pack, but only one is included
specs.spareBattery: Not published by the manufacturer; Shark does not list a price on the product page. Third-party XBATR-series replacements are widely sold
specs.dockOrMount: Charging stand and charging cord included. The PowerDetect auto-empty base is a separate product (IP3251) and cannot be added to this one later
specs.filtration: Sources conflict: SharkNinja lists felt and washable-foam pre-motor filters plus a HEPA post-motor filter, while Abt's spec sheet for the same SKU says 'no HEPA filter'. Shark does not claim its Anti-Allergen Complete Seal on this cordless model, though it does on the corded PowerDetect
specs.binCapacity: 0.7 qt (23.68 oz) dust cup with a bottom-release flap — debris drops out but your hand stays above the opening
specs.maintenance: Foam and felt pre-motor filters are washable and Shark specifies a monthly rinse. Replacement brushrolls and filters are stocked by SharkNinja

pros: The MultiFLEX wand folds so it stands on its own and lies flat under a sofa — Dyson has no equivalent at any price
Push-button power rather than a held trigger, which is the ergonomic complaint people actually leave Dyson over
5-year limited warranty on the unit is by far the longest here
Detection genuinely modulates suction by floor type and dirt level rather than just lighting up an icon
cons: The 70-minute claim is ECO at the bare handheld with no wand or floor head — the honest working figure is much lower and Shark publishes none
Shark publishes neither air watts nor Pa, so this machine cannot be compared on paper against anything else in the category
Sources disagree on whether this SKU even has a HEPA filter, and Shark pointedly does not claim a sealed anti-allergen system on it
One battery in the box and no published spare-battery price
shortTagline: Best-handling stick here, with the vaguest runtime claim and no published suction figure.

material: Plastic body with metal telescopic wand
features: 400 air watts — the highest genuinely comparable suction figure in this category
All-in-One Clean Station charges, stores and auto-empties into a bagged 2 L canister
AI Cleaning Mode 2.0 senses floor type and sets suction automatically
Full published runtime table: 100 min min-power, 49 mid, 16 max, 1 in Jet
10-year motor warranty

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum with a bagged auto-empty Clean Station
specs.suctionRating: 400 air watts. Samsung publishes air watts, so this is directly comparable with Dyson's 240 AW rather than a Pa number
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Samsung publishes the whole table instead of a single best case: 100 minutes on minimum, 49 on mid, 16 on max and 1 minute in Jet mode. The 100-minute headline is the lowest setting
specs.batteryRemovable: Sources conflict: Samsung and RC Willey list the battery as removable, while Abt's spec sheet for the same SKU lists it as non-removable. One battery is included either way
specs.dockOrMount: All-in-One Clean Station included — free-standing, charges, stores tools and auto-empties. Needs roughly 14 inches of floor width
specs.filtration: Multi-cyclonic with HEPA; Samsung claims 99.999% of fine dust captured. The station is bagged, so emptying never exposes you to the dust
specs.binCapacity: 0.5 L on-board bin; 2 L bagged Clean Station, which Samsung says holds up to two months of debris
specs.maintenance: The Clean Station uses disposable dust bags — three in the box, more must be bought, and that is the permanent running cost. On-board filters are washable

pros: 400 air watts, published in the same unit Dyson uses — the strongest honestly comparable number on this page
Samsung publishes a complete per-mode runtime table rather than one best case; almost nobody else in the category does
The bagged Clean Station empties the vacuum for you and keeps your hands out of the dust entirely
10-year motor warranty and full SmartThings integration
cons: Jet mode — the setting that produces the 400 AW headline — runs for one minute
The Clean Station needs about 14 inches of floor width and is loud enough to be a problem near a bedroom
Bags are a permanent consumable; LG's rival tower is bagless
Street price has swung between roughly $500 and $1,100 within a year, and stock has been patchy at Best Buy, Samsung and Abt
shortTagline: 400 air watts, honestly published — and a Jet mode that lasts exactly one minute.

material: Plastic body with telescopic metal wand
features: Two quick-release batteries in the box, both charging in the tower at once
All-in-One Tower auto-empties the bin and is bagless — no dust bags to buy
Kompressor compacts the bin contents, which LG rates at 2.4x usable capacity
5-step filtration with HEPA, plus a separate 3-stage filter in the tower
5.95 lb — the lightest full-size stick vacuum here

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum with a bagless auto-empty charging tower
specs.suctionRating: 210 air watts maximum, per the Home Depot spec sheet. LG's own product page states no suction figure at all
specs.runtimePoweredHead: LG states the condition itself: 'up to 120 minutes' is two 60-minute batteries added together, in Normal mode, without a power nozzle attached. Fit the Dual Floor Max nozzle and the figure drops sharply; LG publishes no per-mode table
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — two quick-release batteries included, and the tower charges both simultaneously
specs.dockOrMount: All-in-One Tower included: free-standing, charges both batteries, stores tools and auto-empties the bin
specs.filtration: 5-step filtration with a HEPA element, LG claims 99.99% of dust; the tower adds a 3-stage filter claimed at 99.9%. LG publishes no whole-machine seal certification
specs.binCapacity: Kompressor compresses the contents — LG claims 2.4x the capacity of a non-Kompressor bin. The tower is bagless
specs.maintenance: Cyclone and filters are removable and washable, so there is no scheduled filter purchase. The bagless tower means no consumable bags either

pros: The only machine here that ships with two batteries, and the tower charges both at once — a genuine 2x working session
The auto-empty tower is bagless, so unlike Samsung's Clean Station there is nothing to keep buying
5.95 lb is the lightest full-size stick vacuum on this page
Kompressor physically compacts the bin contents, so you empty it far less often than a 0.5 L rival
cons: The 120-minute headline is two batteries combined, in Normal mode, with no power nozzle fitted — LG's own footnote says so
210 air watts sits well under Dyson's 240 and Samsung's 400, and LG only publishes it on retailer spec sheets, not its own page
Only 1 year of parts-and-labour cover; the 10-year figure covers the motor alone
LG's US stick line churns fast — the A927 and A929 siblings are already discontinued
shortTagline: Two batteries and a bagless auto-empty tower; 120 minutes means both, with no nozzle.

features: 3-in-1 body: motor unit mounts at the top, at the floor, or comes off as a handheld
Two 25.2 V / 2500 mAh batteries included
HEPA Lifetime filter that Miele states never needs replacing
Multi Floor XXL electrobrush with an LED strip for hidden dust
Free-standing — it does not need a wall or a dock to stay upright

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum, 3-in-1 convertible (top-mount, floor-mount or handheld)
specs.suctionRating: Not published by the manufacturer — Miele publishes three electronic power levels but no air-watt, Pa or motor-watt suction figure
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Miele's own support page gives the real table: 60 minutes at MIN level with the PowerUnit alone (no powered head), falling to 14-17 minutes at maximum power with an electrobrush attached. The '120 minutes' on the box is two 60-minute batteries added together
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — two 25.2 V / 2500 mAh Vortex batteries included, swappable without tools
specs.dockOrMount: Wall mount and charging tray included; there is no floor dock and no auto-empty. The machine free-stands unaided
specs.filtration: Maintenance-free HEPA Lifetime filter, 99.999% dust retention claimed. Miele publishes no whole-machine seal certification
specs.binCapacity: 0.5 L bin with a bottom release
specs.maintenance: The HEPA Lifetime filter is designed never to be replaced, so there is no filter consumable at all. Spare batteries at $229 are the only real running cost

pros: Miele publishes the real runtime table — including 14-17 minutes at max with the electrobrush — where almost every rival publishes only a best case
Two batteries included plus a HEPA filter Miele says never needs replacing: the lowest consumable cost in the category
The 3-in-1 body lets you put the motor at the floor end for stairs or on top for balance, and it stands up on its own
Push-button power, not a held trigger
cons: $1,199 and Miele will not publish a suction figure of any kind, so you cannot compare it on paper with a Dyson or a Samsung
Spare batteries are $229 each — more than twice Dyson's $99.99
No auto-empty tower is offered at any price, unlike LG and Samsung at lower money
The '120 minutes' on the box is two batteries, at minimum power, with no powered head fitted
shortTagline: The most honest runtime figures in the category, on the least published suction.

features: 90 air watts — a genuinely comparable suction figure at a sub-$250 price
Publishes a per-mode runtime table naming the attachment used for each mode
Self-standing body, so the wall bracket is genuinely optional
TripleStrike anti-tangle roller with a mini motorised brush in the box
Detachable 3000 mAh battery that charges on or off the vacuum

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum, converts to handheld
specs.suctionRating: 90 air watts. Levoit publishes air watts, so it is directly comparable with Dyson's 240 AW rather than a Pa figure
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Levoit states the attachment for each figure: 60 minutes in Eco with the crevice tool, 40 minutes in Standard with the vacuum head or motorised brush, and 12 minutes in Turbo. The 60-minute headline is the non-powered tool
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — detachable 3000 mAh pack with three LED cells, charges attached or removed
specs.spareBattery: Not published by the manufacturer. Note the LVAC-200 and LVAC-300 packs are not interchangeable
specs.dockOrMount: Wall-mount bracket included and it needs screws, but the vacuum free-stands without it. No dock and no auto-empty
specs.filtration: 5-stage with a HEPA element, Levoit claiming 99.99% of 0.3-micron particles retained. Levoit makes no sealed-whole-machine claim
specs.binCapacity: 3.2 cups (about 0.76 L) with a bottom release
specs.maintenance: Washable metal pre-filters and a washable HEPA element. Levoit publishes neither a replacement schedule nor a filter price

pros: Publishes air watts and a three-mode runtime table that names the attachment for each figure — unusually honest at this price
Self-standing, so unlike Dyson and Miele you are not obliged to drill a bracket into a wall
Detachable battery that charges off the machine, at a price where sealed packs are the norm
Around $230 street for 90 AW, a HEPA element and a 2-year warranty
cons: 90 air watts is barely a third of the Dyson's 240 — this is a maintenance vacuum, not a deep-carpet one
12 minutes in Turbo, and 40 rather than 60 as soon as the powered head goes on
A HEPA element in a body Levoit never claims is sealed is not an allergy solution
No spare-battery price published, and the LVAC-200 pack will not fit
shortTagline: Publishes air watts and a real per-mode runtime table — at a third of Dyson's suction.

connectivity: No app despite the Wyze name
features: Per-mode suction and per-mode runtime both published — rare at $130
Removable 6-cell 21.6 V battery
Dual motors: 300 W in the body plus a second motor in the brush head
4.9 lb fully assembled
Three modes: Eco 6,000 Pa, Medium 9,000 Pa, Turbo 20,000 Pa

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum, converts to handheld
specs.suctionRating: Sources conflict on units: Wyze quotes 20,000 Pa in Turbo (9,000 Medium, 6,000 Eco) and separately claims '100 AW'. Pa is sealed suction measured at a blocked inlet, not work done at the head, and 100 AW alongside 20,000 Pa is not a figure Wyze substantiates
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Wyze publishes all three modes — 40 minutes Eco, 23 Medium, 10 Turbo — but does not state whether the powered floor head is fitted for any of them
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — removable 6-cell pack (2,000 mAh x 6, 21.6 V DC), 4-6 hours to charge
specs.dockOrMount: Neither. An AC charger only — no wall mount, no dock, no stand in the box
specs.filtration: 3-stage with a filter Wyze calls HEPA but rates at '95% of particles under 0.3 micron'. Genuine HEPA is 99.97% at 0.3 micron. No sealed-system claim
specs.binCapacity: Sources conflict: Wyze's own product page gives 0.55 L in one place and 0.7 L in another
specs.maintenance: Washable filter. Wyze publishes no replacement schedule, no filter price and no brush-roll availability

pros: $129.99 for a removable battery, a motorised head and a published three-mode runtime table
4.9 lb assembled — light enough to carry upstairs one-handed, and the handheld half is 2.8 lb
Publishes suction per mode as well as runtime per mode, which most budget brands avoid
A second motor in the brush head rather than a passive roller
cons: The 'HEPA filter' is rated at 95% of sub-0.3-micron particles. Real HEPA means 99.97%. This is not an allergy vacuum whatever the listing says
No wall mount, no dock, no stand — it ships with a bare AC charger and nowhere to put it
10 minutes in Turbo, and Wyze will not say whether that is with the floor head running
Wyze's own page gives two different bin capacities, which does not inspire confidence in the rest of the sheet
shortTagline: $130 and honest about runtime — but its 'HEPA' filter is rated 95%, not 99.97%.

features: ONEPWR 20 V 4.0 Ah battery shared across Hoover's whole cordless range
1.0 litre dirt cup — roughly three times a typical stick vacuum's
Four power modes with a Tangle Guard brush roll
Upright body that free-stands and swivels
15-cyclone separation with LED headlights

specs.machineType: Dry cordless stick vacuum in upright form — it does not convert to a handheld
specs.suctionRating: Not published by the manufacturer. Hoover quotes '50% more power' than the previous Evolve and a 20 V / 4.0 Ah battery, neither of which is a suction figure
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Hoover's '35 minutes of continuous runtime' is the low suction mode. There are four power modes and Hoover publishes a runtime for none of the other three
specs.batteryRemovable: Yes — and the ONEPWR 20 V pack is shared across Hoover's whole cordless line, including its floor washers and blowers
specs.spareBattery: Not published on the product page; ONEPWR 4.0 Ah packs are stocked as a standard Hoover accessory
specs.dockOrMount: Charger only. The vacuum free-stands. No dock, no wall mount, no auto-empty
specs.filtration: 15-cyclone separation that Hoover rates at 99.4% of dirt and dust, at an unspecified particle size. Hoover makes no HEPA claim and no sealed-system claim
specs.binCapacity: 1.0 L (1 quart) dirt cup, the largest on-board bin here, with a bottom release
specs.maintenance: Washable filter with no published replacement interval. Third-party washable replacements are widely sold, which is what most owners end up buying

pros: The ONEPWR battery fits Hoover's entire cordless range, so a spare pack is useful well beyond this vacuum
A 1-litre dirt cup means far fewer trips to the bin than the 0.5-0.77 L rivals
Upright, self-standing body is easier on the wrist over a long session than a handheld-balanced stick
$280 including a 4.0 Ah pack and a charger
cons: Hoover publishes no suction figure of any kind — not air watts, not Pa, not even motor watts
99.4% filtration at an unstated particle size, no HEPA claim and no sealed system: the wrong machine for allergies
The 35-minute figure is the low mode; three other modes exist and none has a published runtime
Does not convert to a handheld, so above-floor cleaning means hauling the whole upright with you
shortTagline: A litre of bin and a battery that fits everything Hoover makes; no suction figure at all.

model: Tineco FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra
features: Lays flat to 5.1 inches so it slides under sofas and beds
iLoop dirt sensor raises suction and water only where the floor is dirty
FlashDry self-clean with 185°F (85°C) hot-air drying for 5 minutes
DualBlock anti-tangle roller with dual-sided edge cleaning
Forward self-traction so the head pulls itself along

specs.machineType: Cordless wet-dry hard-floor washer — it vacuums and washes sealed hard floors, and is not a carpet vacuum
specs.suctionRating: 21 kPa sealed suction with a 230 W motor rating. Tineco publishes no air-watt figure, so this cannot be compared directly with the dry sticks here
specs.runtimeMax: Not published by the manufacturer — Tineco quotes 50 minutes and does not break it down by Auto, Max or Suction mode
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Unlike a dry stick there is no non-powered-tool inflation here: the roller motor always runs on a washer, so the 50 minutes is the machine as sold. Tineco still publishes no Max-mode figure
specs.batteryRemovable: No — the 7-cell 3,900 mAh pack is internal and not user-swappable
specs.spareBattery: Not applicable — the battery is not user-replaceable
specs.dockOrMount: Charging and self-clean dock included; the machine runs its self-clean cycle sitting in the dock
specs.filtration: A washable dry filter sits over the dirty-water tank. Tineco makes no HEPA claim and no sealed-system claim for this model
specs.binCapacity: 1.0 L clean water tank and a 0.72 L dirty water tank
specs.weight: Not published by the manufacturer for the Stretch Ultra (the older S7 Pro is 11.46 lb)
specs.maintenance: The FlashDry self-clean washes the roller with unheated tank water and then dries it with 185°F (85°C) air for 5 minutes — the 185°F in the marketing is the drying air, not the wash water. Hot-water washing needs the S7 Stretch Steam instead. The dirty-water tank and its hair filter are still emptied and rinsed by hand every time. Tineco specifies one capful of its own solution per tank and advises against third-party detergents

pros: Lays flat to 5.1 inches and goes under furniture — the single reason to pick this over the older S7 Pro
Hot-air drying after every self-clean is what stops the roller going sour between uses
Dual-sided edge cleaning reaches within about a centimetre of a baseboard on both sides
The iLoop sensor throttles suction and water to the actual dirt, which is why 50 minutes is a realistic working figure
cons: The self-clean washes with unheated tank water; only the drying air is 185°F. Hot-water washing costs $150 more on the Stretch Steam
The battery is sealed inside — when the pack dies, the machine dies
Tineco advises against third-party solution, so detergent is a permanent tie to Tineco
You still empty and rinse the dirty-water tank and pick the hair out of its filter by hand after every use
shortTagline: Lays flat under furniture and dries itself hot — but self-cleans with cold water.

features: 356°F steam mode plus a 187°F hot-water wash mode
Self-clean uses 194°F water and 356°F steam, then 203°F hot-air drying
Detachable solid/liquid separation module in the dirty-water tank
22,000 Pa suction with 180° lay-flat and lit AI assistant wheels
Auto detergent dispenser that Roborock rates at about 30 days per fill

specs.machineType: Cordless wet-dry hard-floor washer with steam
specs.suctionRating: 22,000 Pa. Roborock publishes Pa only — there is no air-watt figure, so it is not comparable with the dry sticks
specs.runtimeMax: Not published by the manufacturer. VacuumWars measured roughly 15-25 minutes in the steam and hot-water modes against up to 60 in Auto
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Auto mode is up to 60 minutes. Heating water to 187°F or generating 356°F steam is what actually drains the pack, and Roborock publishes no figure for either — the heated modes are the ones people buy this for
specs.batteryRemovable: Not published by the manufacturer — Roborock does not describe the pack as user-removable
specs.filtration: Washable filters on the dirty-water separation module. Roborock makes no HEPA claim and no sealed-system claim
specs.binCapacity: 1.0 L clean water tank; dirty-water tank with a detachable solid/liquid separation module
specs.maintenance: The only washer here whose self-clean genuinely uses heat: 194°F water and 356°F steam on the roller, then about 5 minutes of 203°F hot-air drying, with anti-scale protection Roborock rates for three years. The dirty tank is still emptied by hand, but the separation module strains the hair out first so your hand stays clear of the slurry. Detergent auto-dispenses from Roborock's own solution; third-party compatibility is not published

pros: The self-clean actually uses heat — 194°F water and 356°F steam on the roller, then 203°F drying — where Tineco's and Bissell's use cold tank water
356°F steam lifts dried-on grease that a plain wet roller simply smears around
The detachable separation module means emptying the dirty tank does not put your fingers into hair slurry
22,000 Pa, 180° lay-flat and an auto detergent dispenser you refill roughly monthly
cons: 12.1 lb is the heaviest machine on this page and you feel it before the tank is empty
Roborock publishes no runtime for the steam or hot-water modes, which are the modes that justify the price
Only a 1-year warranty against Shark's 5 and Miele's 2
No air-watt figure, no HEPA claim, and on carpet it is no substitute for a dry stick vacuum
shortTagline: The only washer here that self-cleans with genuinely hot water and steam.

features: A dedicated dry-vacuum mode with its own Easy Empty dirt bin
ZeroGap edge cleaning right up against a baseboard
Two-tank system: 620 ml clean, 450 ml dirty
Power Vac mode Bissell rates at 75% more suction than the CrossWave X7
One-touch self-clean cycle with a charging dock and tray

specs.machineType: Cordless wet-dry hard-floor washer with a separate dry-vacuum mode
specs.suctionRating: Not published by the manufacturer. Bissell quotes '75% more suction than CrossWave X7' and a 25 V battery — a relative claim and an input voltage, neither of which is a suction figure
specs.runtimePoweredHead: Bissell publishes a single 30-minute figure and states only that it 'varies by mode and usage'. There is no separate figure for Power Vac or Power Mop
specs.batteryRemovable: Not published by the manufacturer — Bissell lists a 25 V rechargeable pack with a 4-hour charge but does not describe it as user-removable
specs.dockOrMount: Charging dock and storage tray included
specs.filtration: Bissell publishes no filtration rating for this model and makes no HEPA claim
specs.binCapacity: 620 ml clean water tank and 450 ml dirty water tank, plus a separate Easy Empty dirt bin for dry mode
specs.maintenance: The one-touch self-clean flushes the brush roll with tank water — Bissell does not claim it is heated, and there is no hot-air drying, so the roller is stored damp. Two 8 oz Bissell formulas are in the box and the machine is built around Bissell's own formulas. Replacement brush rolls and filters are stocked by Bissell

pros: A genuine dry-vacuum mode with its own dirt bin — most washers make you wet-mop dry crumbs
ZeroGap edge cleaning takes the head right up to a baseboard, which the Tineco only manages to about a centimetre
Two-tank design keeps dirty water off the floor and both tanks pull straight out on a lever
The cheapest way into a cordless wet-dry washer from a major brand
cons: The self-clean flushes with cold tank water and there is no hot-air drying, so the roller sits damp — exactly the smell problem Tineco and Roborock spent money solving
30 minutes of runtime with no breakdown by mode, and heavy wet work will not reach it
Bissell publishes no suction figure and no filtration rating whatsoever for this machine
Built around Bissell's own formulas, and the two 8 oz sample bottles run out within a few tanks
shortTagline: The cheapest real cordless floor washer — and it self-cleans with cold water.
